node: Appropriations pass-through to lower-tier defense suppliers and working-capital bottlenecks
summary: Expanded the universe around a financial-plumbing chokepoint rather than a weapons-platform chokepoint. The key thesis is that DoD/Congress mechanisms forcing appropriated dollars, progress payments, supplier financing, or prime-contract cash flow down to lower tiers could disproportionately benefit small and mid-cap aerospace/defense suppliers with large backlogs, long production cycles, and working-capital strain. Reference lane remains the primes and DoD policy context, but this pass focuses on lower-tier public manufacturers where backlog-to-cash conversion and receivables timing may be underappreciated.
